exposure: COVID-19 infection during pregnancy and puerperium
outcome: maternal medical complications (low SpO2, convulsions, pneumonitis, maternal deaths, anemia, hypertensive/chronic liver diseases, hypothyroidism)
obstetric complications (preterm birth, pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, antepartum hemorrhage, postpartum hemorrhage, sepsis)
cohort: The study included 104 pregnant or puerperal mothers with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 infection and their 90 neonates.
finding: COVID-19 infection during pregnancy and puerperium was associated with various maternal medical and obstetric complications including low SpO2, maternal deaths, preterm birth, and pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, while neonates did not test positive for COVID-19, showed no congenital anomalies, and no neonatal deaths were recorded.
mod_finding: Among the deliveries, 63 mothers had vaginal deliveries, the rest had cesarean sections, and 14 mothers had first-trimester terminations.
